cases.description: The output of a pass is the input of the next, so a value naming a value naming a value settles over repeated passes.
Each pass replaces every placeholder in the current text, those an earlier pass introduced included.
A message a host wrote as a plain object reaches the first pass as its serialization, and is interpolated like any other.
A message a host wrote as an array is unescaped like any other, so the backslash its serialization doubled is single in the output.
An escape sequence a value introduces is still an escape sequence on the next pass, so an escaped pair never becomes a placeholder and is removed at the end.
Escape sequences are removed exactly once, so a doubly escaped pair in a value leaves a singly escaped pair, not a placeholder.
Escape sequences are removed after the last pass, so an escaped pair in the message is still an escape while later passes run.
The payload default a missing message takes is text the passes resolve, so its escape sequences are removed at the end.
A value may resolve to text containing a placeholder, which the following pass resolves.
The text an option value resolves to is read by the following pass with what surrounds it, so a brace it contributes completes a placeholder there.
The text an inline default resolves to is read by the following pass with what surrounds it, so a brace it contributes completes a placeholder there.
A payload default may resolve to text containing a placeholder, which the following pass resolves.
A wrapper default may resolve to text containing a placeholder, which the following pass resolves.
A wrapper default a selection falls back to is text the following pass resolves, placeholders included.
The payload default a missing message takes is among what may resolve to text containing placeholders, unlike the key echo.
A construct enclosing another is not a placeholder: the inner one resolves first, and the enclosing one is scanned again over what it resolved to.
A value carrying a closing pair closes the enclosing construct early on the following pass, and the rest is literal text.
A value carrying an opening pair keeps the enclosing construct from deriving when it is scanned again, and both pairs stand as literal text.
